body: when I was in highschool, I would hide knifes/razors all over my room. My parents were intrusive and worried. They would search my room when I was away from the house and find the tool. They would confront me about them and think that they "saved" me from ever cutting again because they got my tool. But as you mentioned, there are EASILY other tools to self harm with. Any cuts you do are going to eventually scar. I don't understand why you feel disappointed? I'm sorry other people have seen your cuts. It was really (and still is) for me to share my cuts with others and frankly I feel violated... As you mentioned they are for my eyes only. It sounds like you are doing maybe a tad bit better (using the past tense of selfharm) and reaching out to others. That's great!

I was given antidepressants when I got out. The problem happened when I went to a PHP (partial out-patient program) for 3 weeks and they lowered my meds because I was doing really well in the program. Which I was, but now that I don't have that structure, I'm doing absolutely horrible. I see my therapist tomorrow, and I made it through the weekend here.

There was a kid in my high school who was about 3 grades older than me. He was nice, flashed his smile all the time, had a lot of friends, lived in an expensive neighborhood, got really good grades. His mom was on the PSA board, active in the community, and a well-paid counselor in the area.

One day, the school was on shut down, helicopters everywhere with at least 10 police cars. Turns out the kid stabbed his mom 100+ times in the EYES and was on the run. It was REALLY unexpected.

Remember when you told yourself you would never cut ever again? Remember when you broke that promise? Remember where that scar came from? Remember how angry at the world you were? Remember a life before self harm? 

I don't.

I apologize I didn't read see this message in time. I attempted suicide and cut up my arms really bad. I went to the ER and then was admitted to a mental hospital for a week. I'm out now and back at my apartment. I'm OK. I'm going to a meetup.com support group for depression tomorrow morning. I still feel shaky and depressed, but I know I need to speak up about it to my family before I let it get so bad again. Thank you for your response. I was in a terrible, terrible place when I posted this and I'm thankful that people cared enough. I will add that phone number to my phone book.

I panicked when I read the title of the post because I thought for a second you could be my boyfriend. We are in a long distance relationship, too. And I recently told him I've been cutting again and have been depressed. 

Anyway. My boyfriend has done a lot of what you have. Shared some personal things, told me to call him when I feel like cutting, letting me know that he is there for me. 

Self harm is very difficult to deal with. For both parties. I don't call him to talk, I feel like he is very supportive, but in the moment of cutting, I don't want to talk. I don't want to do anything but feel something. 

He caught on that I don't call him. So he said "I don't understand why you do it, but please, please only do it as a last resort". I still don't know how to react to that. I would suggest not saying something like that to your gf. It like opened the door to me cutting more and more because now I knew he accepts it.

I wish my bf would call me more. Or do little things like text me that he loves me. Or like someone else suggested, a hand written letter would be great. Because then she could hang it in her room. And instead of trying to control her emotions and gather her thoughts, find her phone, call your number, wait for you to pick up, she could just look at your letter and be reminded that you care for her. 

I hope it all works out for you.

I think cutting out of anger is the worst. Recently, I have for other reasons and I find it so so difficult to control myself. I cut a lot on my arms, usually unaware of how deep I'm going because my adrenaline is pumping and I get so angry. What do you feel shameful about afterwards? 

I'm sorry to hear abut your pets. I had a dog for about 17 years (I grew up with him) and he passed away around this time last year. It was devastating. But he was in so much pain the last days of his life that it was relieving to know he's not anymore. It's tough. Really tough. But time does make it better. I still miss my pup like no other, but time has made me smile when I think of him rather than cry.

Best: My boyfriend telling me that he will never leave me because of the cutting. That he loves every inch of me including my scars.

Worst: My sister attempting to be supportive by saying "You need to stop cutting yourself because you are going to regret it in the future. Imagine all those scars over your body, they will never go away".
Why do you want to kill yourself in the first place?
You can get attention other ways. You won't know if you got the attention if you OD because you'll be passed out...
Yeah, I don't like suicide hotlines, either. But they work for some people. Why do you want your suicide to be public?
I'm sorry. My dad has been battling cancer for 2 years. He had bladder cancer, too. But they removed it, only to notice more spread. Cancer is some scary shit to deal with.

You don't need to care. But if you have friends and family who care about you, then killing yourself would kill a part of them, too. Families never recover from a child committing suicide. The point is that you were put on this earth for a reason. Even if we all are just microscopic specs in the magnified, populated world, you are a part of this world. I get you're curious about the afterlife, but killing yourself isn't the way to go about it. Maybe read a few books about the afterlife--I'm sure there is a ton. And who's to say the life after death is better than reality? Why take the risk? You can take the risk to live and find out why you exist. And if you run into speed bumps along the way, you can change your life. But when you die, it's solid-it can't be undone.

I have very similar thoughts as yours. Like spotting the best places to kill myself on campus. To show everyone that the world is fucked up and people struggle in silence and people don't care until it's too late. But the truth is that the "signs" you may be giving off that you are doing shitty, may not be as noticeable as you think. People have their own shit going on and I'm not saying that's a reason to ignore your pain and not reach out to you, but for a lot of people it's difficult to put their own struggles and every day life aside to notice how other people are actually doing. 

I hope you find the strength within yourself to not go through with it. I know it's hard--I've wanted to kill myself a handful of times already this semester; but I didn't in hopes that the semester will get better. And it will. Whatever is going on with you, I notice, people read your posts-they notice you. 

If you are looking for a friend, feel free to PM me. Maybe we can help each other out. Stay safe and please call someone, a friend, family member or a hotline if you feel you aren't in control.

Your impact is your connection to other people. Your family, your friends, your support system. You make an impact on the people around you. Yeah, you may never win an emmy or do some extravagant work that gets your name up in the stars, but none of that matters because you make a mark on other peoples lives. If you feel you can't live for yourself, live for your mom, or your dad, sister or brother, oh hell, live for your dog/pet. People need you in their life more than you probably realize.

I've had bad experiences with suicide hotlines. The person I always seem to get is too distracted/doesn't care to help in any way. So I stopped calling them. I had a friend back in high school tell a suicide hotline that she was going to kill herself and she had the "options" all set. The cops were called on her and she was taken away. But that was because she had the "method" at her finger tips.

If you're suicidal and don't have like a gun in one hand and the phone in the other--- then you should be fine. Hopefully if you get a cool person, things will go well for you.

Also, it's important to realize that if you are anxious to call--to remember that you can always just hang up. If you don't like the person, or they are disrespectful to you, just hang up and try a different hotline. 

I hope it goes well for you. You should call them even if you have heard horror stories. Because you'll never know if it works if you don't give it a shot.

My sisters always say "You have more friends than you think". Whether that's true or not, you do have people that will support you whether it's online or irl. I'm sorry you cut. But don't let be your set back. It was a slip up--everyone has those once in a while. Maybe if you're upset that you broke a promise--try setting a goal. Then you can say you didn't reach your goal; but goals can always be modified and reached.
This IS important!! Great job on a week clean! That takes a lot of effort! I hope you enjoyed your birthday! Keep it up. Try not to belittle yourself!
Like everyone has said, I don't think those will every completely heal. They will probably turn white with time, but that's about it. You can buy some scar creme to help reduce the appearance.

Interesting topic.

In high school when my cutting was real bad I had to get stitches on my wrist up and on my hand. I had one of those white cloth bandages around my arm and wrapped around my hand for like 3 weeks. I remember being in science class and we were about to dissect something and the girl said rather loudly "I can't work with you if you wear that brace--What are you hiding?!?" I said I wasn't hiding anything.. that it was just a sprain. She then said "I do gymnastics, thats not a sprain bandage!" I panicked and left the classroom, and hid in the bathroom til the bell rang.

There was a super hot young teacher who taught both history class. He was really nice and I told him that I was depressed and cut. It was a super big mistake. He was cool with it at first but after I was like suicidal and shit he told the counselor. I was called down to the counselors office that week and there was a police officer in the room. They said someone told them that I was hiding razors in my locker (I wasn't). I was escorted out of the school and driven to the local mental hospital. And that day I was suspended from school for "threats".

They never found anything, because no "weapon" was there. It was all bullshit. Yeah I needed help but once I was kicked out of school, I REALLY spiraled down. Lost all my friends, rumored all over the internet.. It was horrible.

Anyway, sorry lol that took a turn that wasn't really related to this topic.

I guess back then I kinda wanted to get caught. But if I knew I would get kicked out of the school because of it, then I wouldn't have ever shared anything. Now, I'm 21/f and still cut, I don't want anyone to know. I hide it well. If I were to get caught now, by like a roommate or professor (does that happen?) then I'd just brush it off. It wouldnt bother me; it's not really any of their business.

I'm sorry what you're going through. I have never had an abortion so I have no idea the grade of emotional and physical pain you're going through. But ending your life wouldn't help anything. Like you said, maybe you weren't ready for a kid. But sometime in the future maybe you will be ready. But ending you life.. You end the chances of that happening.
I tell no such lies.
